To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stimulated emission lines in the 1-0 band of DF were obtained in a chemical DF laser using the D2 + F3NF mixture at a pressure of ~1 tor, the largest number of DF laser lines was obtained using this mixture, the time dependences were measured for the intensities of the various lines, and the results of these measurements are explained.

the largest number and strongest emission lines are obtained in the DF chemical laser utilizing the D 2 + NF 3 mixture, that the time dependences are explained by the features of cascade transitions and the increase of mixture temperature during a reaction.
the chemical lasers utilizing mixtures D2 + Fx, D2 + Fy, D2 + Nx, and D2+Fz are characterized by a high efficiency and by a large number of stimulated emission bands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of the methods of quantum chemistry and spectroscopy for solving problems of laser physics.
the study of chemical reactions and their products.
the development of a chemical laser utilizing the D + F → DF reaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a chemical DF laser is a promising device for the generation of stimulated radiation in the 3- to 5-μm region.
the D2 + F NO2 system is the best of the four systems studied.
the chemical laser utilizing the reaction D2 + F NO2 has the best potential for use as an efficient source of coherent infrared radiation in the range 2.3–2.7 microns.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the D2 + F mixture is not a good candidate for a practical DF chemical laser.
we have shown that the DF laser utilizing the D + NF3 reaction is the most promising of those studied, and that the laser utilizing the reaction D + N2F 4 is also promising.
the chemical laser is capable of producing radiation in the 1.0–1.5 micron range with a high efficiency and a high degree of monochromaticity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DF laser utilizing the D3 + NF3 mixture can be used as a source of radiation for the spectroscopy of the DF molecule.
a mixture of D2 + NF2 can serve as a basis for a chemical laser operating in the range of 3.5–4.5 microns.
the D2 + N 2 F 4 mixture is the most efficient chemical laser system.
